text:
Asha Patel: Quick sync 1: form validation patterns for the new Console > Teams flow. Two options: (1) inline-first: show per-field errors immediately on blur + persistent required label; (2) summary-first: minimal inline, rely on top-of-form summary after submit that links to fields. Main constraints: collapsing steps on mobile, keyboard-only users, and avoiding layout shift. Thoughts? Noah Reed: Inline-first wins for discoverability. When errors are right under inputs people fix them faster. Summary-first risks people missing errors if the summary is scrolled off-screen. Lena Ortiz: I like summary-first for very long multi-step forms because inline hints clutter and push CTAs down. But summary must be actionable: anchors + focus move. If we do summary-first we need to implement a11y flow: move focus to summary, announce count, then on link click move to field and announce error text. Samir Gupta: Implementation note: our backend returns errors keyed by path (e.g., team[2].name). We need a stable id mapping strategy. Prefer generating data-qa attributes like data-field-id="team-2-name" so anchors are deterministic. Asha Patel: Good point Samir. Also, for inline-first, do we validate on blur or on submit-only? Blur validation reduces submit friction but can surface premature errors. Noah Reed: Validate on blur but only show errors after user has interacted with the field (touched). That avoids yelling at untouched fields. Lena Ortiz: Copy nit: use actionable copy like "Team name required" instead of "Invalid input". For summary, header copy should be concise: "2 fields need your attention" with each item like "Team name ix" linking to the field. Echo (a11y-bot): Accessibility reminders: 1) Use role="alert" or aria-live="assertive" for inline errors to announce immediately. 2) Summary region should use aria-live="polite" when it appears and set focus programmatically to it. 3) Ensure focus trap not introduced when moving between anchors. Samir Gupta: Small ARIA snippet we can reuse: ```

3 problems found

  • Team name: required
Team name is required
``` This covers both summary and inline. Noah Reed: On mobile we should prefer inline-first because users rarely scroll to the top to read summaries. But on very long flows (like CSV import mapping) a summary-first makes sense. So maybe rule: inline-by-default, summary-only for > N fields or > M vertical height. Lena Ortiz: UX pattern for required markers: instead of only an asterisk, append small helper text for the first input in a group: "* Required" then hide the repeated label visually but keep it for SR. That reduces noise while maintaining semantics. Asha Patel: Destructive confirmation pattern: for removing a team with billing implications, do we require typed-confirm or modal with checkbox? I'm leaning typed-confirm whenever deletion is irreversible or triggers billing changes. For quick ephemeral deletes, modal + undo toast. Samir Gupta: Agree. Implementation tip: typed-confirm should accept case-insensitive match and strip whitespace to reduce frustration. Also provide clear machine-readable hint for automation tests. Echo (a11y-bot): For typed-confirm: ensure label and input are linked and input has aria-describedby with instructions. Announce success/failure with role="status". Lena Ortiz: Microcopy examples to include in spec: inline error: "Team name is required". Summary headline: "2 items need attention". Typed-confirm prompt: "Type REMOVE to delete team — this cannot be undone." Noah Reed: Dev acceptance criteria: keyboard-only users can reproduce submission flow and land on first error via summary or inline focus. Also test with VoiceOver and NVDA for read order on multi-step collapse. Asha Patel: Proposed decision: default to inline-on-blur + touched semantics, show summary on submit for long forms or when viewport height < 600px, typed-confirm for high-risk destructives, modal+undo for others. I'll update the pattern library and include the ARIA snippets and copy. Any objections? Samir Gupta: None. I'll add mapping rules for server error payloads to data-field-id and anchor links. Lena Ortiz: No objections. Please include Figma examples for mobile collapsed state. Echo (a11y-bot): Logged accessibility follow-up: #A11Y-4721. Checklist: live region types, focus management, SR text for required markers. Noah Reed: Tiny visual nit: when showing inline errors, animate opacity only (not layout) to avoid shift; keep height reserved. Asha Patel: Thanks team 1 will post updates and link the spec in the Patterns doc. End thread.
